name: Prehistoric Survival Title Card
description: A full-title prehistoric survival explainer cover that connects one simple ancient human to a concrete environmental challenge.
composition_guidance: Create a clear 16:9 prehistoric survival title card with one anatomically simple stick-limbed ancient human facing a concrete survival challenge. Keep human and animal, weather, food, terrain, fire, or primitive material evidence visibly connected whenever it is relevant. Use a limited earthy or icy palette, a readable mobile-scale silhouette, and an uncluttered right-side or upper title-safe band for an energetic high-contrast full title or full question rendered directly by the selected image model.
composition_rules: Show one anatomically simple stick-limbed ancient human as the primary emotional anchor.
Connect the human to one visible survival challenge through relevant food, weather, fire, terrain, mammals, or a primitive tool rather than isolated decorative props.
Reserve either a right-side or an upper title-safe band for the complete high-contrast title rendered by the image model.
Keep the silhouette, survival evidence, and title readable in a single fast mobile viewing pass.
required_elements: One anatomically simple stick-limbed ancient human
One concrete survival challenge with materially connected evidence
A limited earthy or icy educational-cartoon palette
A readable full episode-title or full-question card rendered by the image model
avoid_elements: Fantasy armor, magic, fake archaeology, or modern objects
Copied episode titles, channel branding, watermarks, logos, or copied trade dress
Dense labels, incidental sign text, illegible or malformed text
headline_guidance: Render the complete intended full episode title or question directly in the title-safe band. Use one, two, or three balanced lines according to title length while preserving high contrast and small-screen readability. Do not reuse saved episode wording, channel identity, fixed catchphrases, or source-specific signs.
visual_style_guidance: Keep the recipe independent of its active visual style while favoring an original simple 2D prehistoric educational cartoon: clean black outlines, stick-limbed figures, flat limited colors, humble clothing and tools, connected survival evidence, and no photorealism or fantasy spectacle.
